facts.content: Patient presents with a headache.
Patient reports an acute new-onset left-occipital headache that started yesterday mid-morning.
facts.source_text: Acute new-onset left-occipital headache started yesterday mid-morning

facts.content: The headache is severe with an intensity of approximately 8 out of 10.
The headache is throbbing in character.
The headache built up gradually.

The patient reports no photophobia with the headache.
The patient reports no vision changes with the headache.
facts.source_text: No nausea/vomiting, photophobia, vision changes, or fever.

facts.source_text: No nausea/vomiting, photophobia, vision changes, or fever.

facts.content: The patient reports no neck stiffness.

facts.content: Assessment is an acute new-onset unilateral left-occipital headache of severity 8 out of 10 with onset yesterday.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute new-onset unilateral left-occipital headache, 8/10, onset yesterday;

facts.content: No red flags are identified from the history, including absence of fever, vomiting, rash, neck stiffness, or reported neurological deficits.
facts.source_text: no red flags identified from history (no fever, vomiting, rash, neck stiffness, or neuro deficits reported).

facts.content: Plan is to start a slightly stronger NSAID analgesic similar to ibuprofen to be taken regularly with meals and not concurrently with ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: Analgesia: start a slightly stronger analgesic similar to ibuprofen ( NSAID) to be taken regularly with meals; do not take at the same time as ibuprofen.

facts.content: Paracetamol can be taken in addition as an adjunct for pain control.
facts.source_text: Adjunct: paracetamol can be taken in addition.

facts.content: Supportive care includes rest and good hydration.
facts.source_text: Supportive care: rest and good hydration.

facts.content: Patient is advised to monitor for red flags such as fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or recurrent episodes and to make contact if these occur or if pain continues or worsens.
facts.source_text: Safety/education: monitor for red flags—fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness—or recurrent episodes; contact if these occur or if pain continues/worsens.

facts.content: A prescription for an alternative NSAID to be taken with food will be provided with instructions to avoid concurrent timing with ibuprofen.
facts.source_text: Rx: provide prescription for an NSAID alternative (to be taken with food) and instructions to avoid concurrent ibuprofen timing.

facts.content: If pain is not settling within 24 to 48 hours, worsens, or new symptoms develop, the patient should contact for further planning.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: if pain not settling within 24–48 hours or worsens, or if new symptoms develop, contact for further planning;

facts.content: Follow-up includes pharmacy pickup of the prescribed medication.
